# Leaf study: evidence and limits

## What is actually reproduced

The unmodified MIT tsoding/leaf-venation main.c, commit 3d828c51d99be86c538769f19f715f919bba5456, is executed with a declared headless drawing backend and deterministic random input. The independent JavaScript port is compared at every step. 64 steps, 846 final nodes, maximum numerical difference 5.0000006e-7. The original Raylib GUI was not run.

The MIT aj-dev-smith/canalisation leaf engine, commit 27ffafcb824d427d994161c6a5122294b152139b, was also executed without edits. Original seed-7 hierarchy and venation harnesses mature at step 2302. The selected visible graph has 410 edges, 41 connected components and 7 independent cycles. These results are evidence of an original executable, not proof of a complete natural leaf or suitability for the reference artwork. It has not been inserted into the rendering model.

## Closed reticulation

The thin-leaf candidate now uses an independent implementation of the closed-growth rules in Runions et al., Modeling and visualization of leaf venation patterns, 2005, sections 3–4. Its initial midrib and secondary scaffold are art-directed constraints. The finest topology is generated by relative-neighbour attraction, delayed tagged-source removal, and explicit bounded welding of reached fronts. It is not a translation of the restricted-license Jason Webb implementation and is not the original authors' executable.

The current fixed seed generates one connected component, 81,513 nodes, 91,440 edges and 9,928 independent cycles. There are 76 unreached sources. The accelerated relative-neighbour query was compared to brute force on 100 randomized inputs. The graph is a study result; no biological calibration or original-author parameter equivalence is claimed.

## Optics

The color map contains green lamina variation, not black painted vein lines. A separate linear field encodes explicitly assumed tissue thickness in millimetres. Absorption varies by thickness and angle to the light, with RGB coefficients [20, 9, 27] per mm. Major veins also have raised 3D geometry. These coefficients and diameters are study parameters, not measurements of the reference leaf.

The browser material uses a thin-wall diffuse transmission approximation and alpha compositing. It is not Karma, a spectral renderer, multi-bounce subsurface scattering, or an interference simulation. Chromatic edge treatment is a separate postprocess toggle. Transparent-layer shadowing remains approximate.

## Visual reference

ImageTinys' supplied video is a visual reference only. Its original Houdini project, exact optical mechanism, lighting, shader graph and color grade have not been obtained. The original images and video are not published with this source.

Visual acceptance: false. AAA production acceptance: false. The R02 browser implementation passed technical tests but was rejected on visual fidelity; R09 is a new candidate requiring fresh real-browser screenshots.

R07 adds two successively denser source-growth passes (420 sources, then 3,800) to create tertiary and fine vein calibre hierarchy. This is an explicit independent growth schedule, not an author parameter match. The original teacher C baseline is unchanged.

R09 refines the network in three passes (420 / 3,800 / 14,000 sources). Degree-two chains are faired while branch junctions stay fixed. Major paths use 80 samples per secondary. A final planar-contact construction splits both edges at each crossing: 420 distinct junctions are welded, and a second independent contact scan finds zero unjoined proper crossings. None of these explicit extensions are claimed as the original reference author implementation.

R09 curves the entire ribbon basis with its spine: edge fold and camber displace along the local normal, with bounded torsion and lateral spine bend differing between the three leaves. This corrects the earlier world-Z camber error, rather than merely rotating the whole object.
